lines.text: A great white shark seized this man around the chest.
South Australia, 1963. A spearfishing championship at Aldinga Beach.
Rodney Fox had no tank. He dived on a single breath.
The jaws closed around him and wouldn't let go.
He reached for the shark's eyes. It released him.
Then it came back and seized his float.
He fought free of the line.
He was pulled out, barely alive.
It took four hundred and sixty-two stitches to close the wounds.
Fox still wanted to go back in the water.
Steel between him and the jaws.
From that cage, Ron Taylor filmed great whites underwater.
Some of the first footage of its kind.
He ran cage-diving trips for decades.
He co-founded a foundation to study and protect great whites.
The shark that nearly killed him turned him into its defender.
